title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is page 70 of an English typescript in a Russian-to-English translation style, with handwritten formulas. The idioms 'at n ≥ n_0', 'Evidently, there exists such n′ that', and the bracket notation O_V[nE] for the sheaf of a divisor point to this. It was filed in the 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' folder. The previous page (French notes on G_R-varieties) and the next page (a title page) are unrelated to it.

The content is the classical inductive proof of Serre vanishing for an ample (hyperplane) divisor E on a projective variety V:
1. Let E_φ be a hyperplane section linearly equivalent to E.
2. Let K be the structure sheaf of E_φ (the cokernel of O_V(-E_φ) → O_V).
3. By induction on dimension, applied to the hyperplane section, there is n_0(K) with H^i(V, K[nE]) = 0 for i ≥ 1 and n ≥ n_0(K).
4. Twist 0 → O_V(-E_φ) → O_V → K → 0 by nE and take the long exact cohomology sequence. The segment H^i(O_V(-E_φ)[nE]) → H^i(O_V[nE]) → H^i(K[nE]) = 0 shows the first map is surjective.
5. Hence dim H^i(O_V[nE]) ≤ dim H^i(O_V(-E_φ)[nE]).
6. Since O_V(-E_φ) ≅ O_V[-E], the right-hand sheaf is O_V[(n-1)E].
7. So the function n ↦ dim H^i(V, O_V[nE]) is non-increasing for n ≥ n_0. The page breaks off just as it begins the next step.

The next step is the standard one: the dimensions must eventually be constant. One then uses the term H^{i-1}(K[nE]) and the surjectivity of H^0(O_V[nE]) → H^0(K[nE]) for large n to get injectivity, and concludes vanishing.

It serves a vanishing/finiteness lemma in a text on algebraic varieties or surfaces, possibly a translated Soviet seminar text such as the Shafarevich school's 'Algebraic Surfaces' (1965). That identification is unsure.
errors: No mathematical error. The inequality follows correctly from surjectivity in the exact sequence. The argument is incomplete on this page because it continues on the next page of the original text, which is not in this folder.

ideas.what: Inductive proof via hyperplane section that H^i(V, O(nE)) is non-increasing in n and eventually vanishes for i ≥ 1
ideas.modern_name: Serre vanishing theorem (Enriques–Severi–Zariski lemma); hyperplane-section induction argument
ideas.where_published: EGA III §2 (cohomology of projective morphisms, Serre's theorem in general form)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of a standard textbook argument (Serre vanishing by hyperplane induction), apparently from a translated typescript not written by Grothendieck and misfiled among the motif notes. It contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: First line reads 'at n ≥ n_0(K)'; the image shows a garbled ≥ symbol.
The last formula should read O_V[(n-1)E]; the handwriting resembles [[n-1]E], but the intended sheaf is O_V[(n-1)E] as in the preceding line.
The bottom-left marginal number '187' is the archive page number, not part of the text.
